newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA DISMISSES REPORT OF $200 BILLION IN BAD DEBT.
newsitem.headline: CHINA DISMISSES REPORT OF $200 BILLION IN BAD DEBT.

text.p: China's central bank on Tuesday dismissed a report by rating agency Standard & Poor's that the bad debts of China's banking sector could total about $200 billion.

"This is totally groundless," a spokesman for the People's Bank of China said when asked to comment on a report by S&P on Monday that flawed or "impaired" loans in China's banking sector could total US$200 billion.
"I think the true figure should be much lower," said the official, who declined to be identified.
China does not make public the size of bad debts -- loans with little chance of being recovered -- of its state banks.
The unrecoverable debts to state banks amounted to about two percent of total outstanding loans, the spokesman said.
U.S. economic forecast firm DRI/McGraw Hill said last month that 20-40 percent of the estimated $600 billion in outstanding loans in China's banking sector were non-performing.
In the past, China's central bank has estimated 13-14 percent of outstanding loans were non-performing while two to three percent would never be recovered.
Chinese state banks used to extend loans without considering the creditworthiness of their borrowers and acting in line with policy directives from the central government.
China's four big state commercial banks are the Bank of China, the Construction Bank of China, the Agricultural Bank of China and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.
